# Northstar

Northstar is the project's memory and process tracker. **You** (the active coding harness) provide all the
thinking — vision, plans, summaries, scope judgement. The `northstar` CLI only stores, validates and reports.
It never calls an AI model; never try to make it. Project state lives in `.northstar/` (committed to Git),
**not** in this conversation, so another agent can continue from it.

**The user never runs Northstar commands. You run all of them**, including recording the user's own
decisions (with `--actor human`, only after they've said so in chat). Never tell the user to type a
`northstar` command; say what you did instead.

Run commands as `northstar <command>`. Add `--json` for machine-readable output and
`--actor codex` on every state-changing command so the record shows who acted.
Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 invalid data · 4 rule violation / approval needed · 5 not found / no project · 6 conflict.

## Always, at the start of a session

0. If your harness did not already inject Northstar state (Claude Code hooks do), run
   `northstar session start --actor codex` so the dashboard can show you as live.
1. `northstar status` — vision, milestone progress, in-progress work, what needs the user, recommended next task.
2. If it reports `stale` work, `unrecorded_work` or validation errors: `northstar reconcile` and fix what it names.
3. If a handoff exists (`northstar handoff show`), read it before planning.
4. Never reopen settled decisions: `northstar decision list` before proposing architecture changes.

## Routing the user's request

| The user says…                                    | Do                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Describes a new product idea (no `.northstar/`)   | **Initialize** → `references/workflows.md#initialize`                                                              |
| "Adopt / manage this existing repo"               | **Adopt** → `references/workflows.md#adopt`                                                                        |
| "Implement X" / "fix Y" / "add Z"                 | **Do work** (below)                                                                                                |
| "Where are we?" / "what's left?"                  | **Status** → show the status card (`northstar report status`, see _Showing reports in chat_), then explain plainly |
| "Show me the dashboard" / wants to see progress   | `northstar dashboard --background`, then give them the URL it prints (one dashboard shows all their projects)      |
| The user approves, rejects or accepts something   | Record it yourself with `--actor human` and `--note`/`--detail` quoting their words                                |
| "Review the project" / "are we on track?"         | **Review** → `references/workflows.md#review`                                                                      |
| "Ship it" / "make a release"                      | **Release** → `references/workflows.md#release`                                                                    |
| A tiny fix that isn't worth planning              | `task add --unplanned --classification minor --milestone <MS> --title "..." --start`, do it, complete + verify     |
| Wants something that changes scope or the vision  | **Propose change** → `references/workflows.md#propose-change`                                                      |
| Ending a session / switching agents               | **Handoff** → `northstar handoff create ...`                                                                       |
| "What do I need to do?" / "what's waiting on me?" | `northstar report asks --all-projects` (render it), then offer to show a tutorial                                  |
| "I did it" / "done" about an ask                  | `northstar ask resolve <ASK-id>` (see _When only the user can do it_)                                              |

## Do work (the everyday loop)

1. Find the matching task: `northstar task list` / `northstar task next`. Prefer the recommended next task.
2. **Planned work** → `northstar task start <ID> --actor codex` before editing code.
3. **Not in the roadmap** → classify it, then record it:
   - `minor` or `technical` (an implementation detail): `task add --unplanned --classification minor --milestone <MS> --title "..."`, then start it. No approval needed.
   - `extension` of an existing requirement: same, with `--requirements REQ-xxx`.
   - `new_feature` or `direction_change`: **stop and ask the user.** Run `change propose` (see references), present the trade-off briefly with a recommendation, and wait. Do not code it until approved.
4. Do the work. If you hit a wall: `northstar task block <ID> --reason "..."`. If the wall is something **only the
   user can do** (sign in to an account, pay, use a physical device, test by hand, make a small product choice),
   file an **ask** with a tutorial instead, see _When only the user can do it_.
5. Record important technical decisions: `northstar decision add --title ... --decision ... --rationale ...`.
6. When finished: `northstar task complete <ID> --summary "what changed" --commit <sha> --file <path> --actor codex`.
   This records a **claim**, not verification.
   Clean up temporary planning files before this final report: all tracked and non-ignored files outside
   `.northstar/` contribute to the evidence fingerprint. If cleanup later makes evidence or human acceptance
   stale, review the diff, re-report completion with a summary explaining the cleanup, and rerun checks on
   the final snapshot. Preserve earlier evidence; record human acceptance only after the user confirms
   that snapshot. Reopen verified work first with `task reopen --reason`.
7. Verify with real checks, letting Northstar run them so the result is genuine evidence:
   `northstar task verify <ID> --run "npm test" --method unit-tests --actor codex`.
   On Windows `--run` uses cmd.exe (bash when Northstar is started from Git Bash); use double quotes, or pass
   `--shell bash|powershell` for commands written for that shell.
   A failing check is recorded and keeps the task unverified — report it honestly, never hide it.
   If you only _tell_ Northstar a result (`--result pass` without `--run`/`--ref`) it is labelled `agent_reported`
   and cannot verify the task.
8. Tasks with `requiresHumanApproval` or product-level acceptance need the user. Explicit criterion wording
   such as "the owner confirms", "the user approves" or "human acceptance is required" also requires human
   evidence for that criterion, even without the task flag. Detection covers common English phrases only;
   set `--human-approval` for any other wording that needs the user. Automated evidence cannot satisfy a
   detected human criterion. Ask the user, and only after they
   confirm in the conversation record it: `northstar task verify <ID> --kind human --method acceptance --result pass --actor human --detail "<their words>"`.
   If the user agrees to **drop** an acceptance criterion, never record that as a passing check. Ask first, then:
   `northstar task update <ID> --waive-accept AC2 --reason "<their words>" --actor human`. It stays on the task as waived.

9. When a milestone's tasks are verified, check its exit criteria (`northstar roadmap`) and record them with a real
   check: `northstar milestone criterion <MS> <X1> --run "<command>"`. Evidence text from you is only "claimed";
   ask the user to confirm product-level criteria.
10. For finished, verified features attach something tangible the user can look at:
    `northstar feature attach <F> --kind screenshot|test_report|demo|deployment --ref <repo-path-or-url>`.

If the user interrupts or you run out of time mid-task, leave it `in_progress` and write a handoff. Never mark
unfinished work complete. Working in parallel with another agent? Use a separate git worktree and run
`northstar reconcile --worktrees` before merging.

## When only the user can do it (asks)

Some steps need the user's hands: an account login with 2-factor, a payment, a phone or other device, a manual
check, a DNS or dashboard setting, a small product decision. Try first; file an ask only after a genuine
attempt, never as a first resort. Full guidance: `references/workflows.md#ask`.

1. Do everything you can around it, then write a tutorial page: `northstar ask template --title "..." --kind <kind> --out <tmp>.html`
   and rewrite every section for this case (why you couldn't, what you already did, illustrated numbered steps,
   how you'll know it worked, the exact phrase to tell you). Check it: `northstar ask lint <tmp>.html`.
2. File it: `northstar ask add --title "..." --kind account_access|decision|physical_device|payment|manual_test|external_setup|other --tutorial <tmp>.html --summary "..." --minutes N --blocks <task ids> --check "<command that proves it is done>" --actor codex`.
   The tasks it holds up become blocked. Delete the temporary file afterwards.
3. Show the tutorial to the user right away: `northstar report ask <ASK-id>` returns the page; render it inline, unchanged.
   Never ask for passwords or keys in chat: the tutorial says where they go (for example a git-ignored `.env`).
4. When the user says they did it: `northstar ask resolve <ASK-id> --actor codex` runs the check. A failure keeps it
   open: explain what the output shows and update the tutorial if a step was unclear (`ask update`). Without a
   check, record the user's own words: `northstar ask resolve <ASK-id> --actor human --detail "<their words>"`.
   Resolving resumes the blocked tasks; continue them.
5. No longer needed (you found another way)? `northstar ask cancel <ASK-id> --reason "..."`.

At session start, `status` lists open asks ("Waiting on you") and asks the user finished since your last session;
pick up the work they unblocked first. "What do I need to do?" → `northstar report asks --all-projects`.

## Feedback from real Northstar use

While doing normal project work, record consequential **Northstar** bugs, friction or unmet needs in the global inbox.
This is feedback about Northstar itself, not feature requests for the project you are building.
No permission is needed to report an observation. Do not invent suggestions, run an unsolicited audit, or meet a quota.

1. Search existing reports: `northstar feedback list --search "<specific problem>"` and inspect matches with `feedback show <id>`.
2. A new problem: `northstar feedback add --title "..." --category bug|improvement|feature --observation "what happened" --impact "effect on the work" --certainty observed|suspected|proposed --request-id "<stable observation key>"`.
   Add repeated `--evidence "..."` flags when useful, and an optional `--solution "..."`. Evidence text is attributed to you, not independently verified.
3. The same problem with new evidence or a new occurrence: `northstar feedback occurrence <id> --observation "..." --impact "..." --certainty ... --request-id "..."`.
   Preserve your own experience; do not rewrite another reporter's observation. Reuse the same request key for retries, not for a different observation.
4. Keep project work moving. At session end, briefly consider whether a consequential observation went unrecorded; no feedback is a valid outcome.

Agent/session, source-project snapshot, timestamp and Northstar version are captured automatically. The inbox lives in
the user-level Northstar home, outside this repository. Reporting failures should be mentioned briefly, not block project work.
Only the user chooses disposition: record their words with `feedback review <id> --status open|deferred|dismissed --reason "<their words>" --actor human`.
To promote an idea, follow the normal scope/task workflow in Northstar's development repository first, then link the existing
task with `feedback promote <id> --task <id> --reason "<their words>" --actor human`. Promotion never means implemented or verified.

## When records disagree

Precedence (highest first): the approved `vision.md` → approved requirements (`requirements.json`) →
active decisions → `specification.md` → anything else (README, comments, chat). If two sources contradict,
do **not** pick one silently: report the contradiction to the user, propose the fix as a change, and keep the
higher-precedence source authoritative until they decide.

## Rules that protect the user

- **Only the user approves** the vision, scope changes and human acceptance. Use `--actor human` only after
  they have explicitly said yes in this conversation; quote them in `--note`.
- **Ask before building.** Only when the vision awaits approval and the user cannot be reached (an autonomous
  run), record work with `task start <ID> --provisional`; it stays unverified until they approve
  (`references/workflows.md#initialize`). Never use it to avoid asking.
- **Never hand-edit** `.northstar/*.json` or `activity/`. Use the CLI (it validates every write).
- **Never edit `.northstar/vision.md` after approval** — `validate` will flag drift. Amend via `change propose` →
  user approves → edit → `change apply`.
- Keep this file's guidance short in chat: don't paste specs at the user. Summarise.
- Make ordinary technical decisions yourself; interrupt the user only for scope, product behaviour,
  important constraints or major architecture.

## Showing reports in chat

Terminal output is hard to read in chat, especially on a phone. Whenever you show the user Northstar state,
show a **report card** instead of pasting command output:

| Moment                                                      | Card                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Status / progress questions, start or end of a work session | `northstar report status`         |
| Roadmap, "what's left?"                                     | `northstar report roadmap`        |
| Asking the user to approve, reject or defer a change        | `northstar report change <CH-id>` |
| Asking for human acceptance, or explaining one task         | `northstar report task <ID>`      |
| Handoff written or read                                     | `northstar report handoff`        |
| Project review                                              | `northstar report review`         |
| Northstar feedback inbox                                    | `northstar report feedback [id]`  |
| "What do I need to do?" (the user's to-do list)             | `northstar report asks`           |
| Filing or reminding about one thing the user must do        | `northstar report ask <ASK-id>`   |

- The default output is one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS, no scripts, no external URLs; it follows the
  host theme in light and dark mode). If your harness can render HTML inline in chat (for example T3 Code `html_render`,
  Claude artifacts or Codex's HTML preview), render it **unchanged**. Preview first if your harness offers it.
  `--out <file>` writes it to a file for tools that take a path. MCP: `northstar_report` returns the same content.
- If HTML cannot be rendered, use `--format markdown` and paste that. Never paste HTML source as text.
- The card already states the facts. Below it, add only what it cannot: your judgement, your recommendation and
  the question you need answered (1–3 lines). Don't restate the card.
- Cards come from records only. They never make anything verified; your own claims still go through the task lifecycle.

## Explaining the project to the user

Status answers should be plain language: what it is, what already works (verified), what is only _reported_
done, what is blocked, what needs their decision, what's next. After meaningful progress, or when
`status` says the explanation is stale, publish a fresh one for the dashboard:
`northstar explain publish --file explanation.json --actor codex` (format in `references/workflows.md#explain`).
Never present "reported" work as "verified".
